rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial noun for a place where someone regularly hangs out.

example.english: We go to this cha chaan teng all the time; it's our usual haunt.
example.traditional: 我哋成日去呢間茶記，係我哋嘅蒲點。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 seng4 jat6 heoi3 ni1 gaan1 caa4 gei3 hai6 ngo5 dei6 ge3 pou4 dim2

rows.note: Use this when referring to a familiar usual place, especially one already known to the listener.

example.english: See you at the usual haunt at seven tonight.
example.jyutping: gam1 maan5 cat1 dim2 lou5 dei6 fong1 gin3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when a memory or past event troubles someone.

example.english: This experience continues to haunt me.
example.jyutping: ni1 dyun6 ging1 lik6 zung6 kwan3 jiu2 gan2 ngo5

rows.note: Use this when a disturbing memory or thought persistently will not go away.

example.english: The shadow of that accident continues to haunt me.
example.traditional: 嗰次意外嘅陰影一直揮之不去。
example.jyutping: go2 ci3 ji3 ngoi6 ge3 jam1 jeng2 jat1 zik6 fai1 zi1 bat1 heoi3

rows.note: Use this for saying that a place is haunted by ghosts.

example.english: Ghosts really haunt this old house.
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 gau6 uk1 zan1 hai6 naau6 gwai2

rows.note: Use this when the ghosts themselves repeatedly appear in or visit a place.

example.english: They say ghosts haunt that hill at night.
example.traditional: 聽講夜晚有鬼喺嗰座山出沒。
example.jyutping: teng1 gong2 je6 maan5 jau5 gwai1 hai2 go2 zo6 saan1 ceot1 mut6
